notes: The same first log line showed up on a second host within ten minutes.
The alarm returned to OK after the change and stayed quiet for the next hour.
A page last month started with this same error text.
No customer payload was copied into this note.
Only one route was affected. The health check stayed green.
The on-call note says the failure started just after the last deploy.

entries.title: Missing order returns 500
entries.happened: An unknown order id looks up None and then reads order.total, which raises AttributeError.
detail: Known order ids still return 200. Only ids missing from the map fail.
The traceback points at the order lookup, not at the database client.
entries.fix: Return HTTP 404 when the order is not in the map. A database timeout or an out-of-memory crash needs a different fix.

entries.title: Unknown coupon returns 500
entries.happened: Checkout indexes the coupon table with a code that is not there, so it raises KeyError.
detail: SPRING50 is the code used in the demo. Any unknown code fails the same way.
A known coupon still discounts the total and returns 200.
entries.fix: Reject an unknown coupon with HTTP 400. This is a code change. A payment-provider outage is a dependency.

entries.title: Checkout with an empty sku
entries.happened: An empty sku is passed into the catalog lookup and the handler raises TypeError while formatting the line item.
detail: The request has no sku query parameter.
The catalog itself is healthy for SKU-1.
entries.fix: Return HTTP 400 when sku is missing. Do not treat this as a catalog outage.

entries.title: Order list drops the last page
entries.happened: The page loop uses range(len(orders)) and stops one short, so the last order is never returned.
detail: Page 1 looks fine when the account has one order.
The missing row is always the final order id in the map.
entries.fix: Include the last index in the page slice. This is an off-by-one in this repo, not a dropped database row.

entries.title: Paid orders reported as failed
entries.happened: A captured payment is mapped to status failed because the handler compares the provider string with the wrong constant.
detail: The provider returned captured. The handler stored failed.
No exception is thrown. The bug is the status value.
entries.fix: Map the captured provider status to paid. Latency on the legacy provider is a separate dependency issue.

entries.title: Checkout retry charges twice
entries.happened: A retried checkout ignores the idempotency key and creates a second payment.
detail: The client sent the same key twice after a timeout.
Both calls returned 201 with different payment ids.
entries.fix: Store the idempotency key and return the first payment on a retry. This is a code defect in checkout.

entries.title: Catalog serves yesterday's price
entries.happened: The price cache never expires, so a price update in the table is invisible until the process restarts.
detail: The table has the new price. The response still has the old one.
A fresh process returns the new price immediately.
entries.fix: Set a short TTL on the price cache, or drop the cache for this lookup. The table write itself succeeded.

entries.title: Daily report misses the last hour
entries.happened: The report window is computed in UTC and then compared with local timestamps, so the last hour of the day is omitted.
detail: Rows exist in the log for that hour.
The export for days=90 can also run out of memory. That is a separate resource incident.
entries.fix: Compare both ends of the window in one timezone. Do not raise the Lambda memory for a missing hour.

entries.title: ORDERS_TABLE missing after deploy
entries.happened: A deploy removed the ORDERS_TABLE environment variable. Every request fails at startup with KeyError.
detail: The previous version still had ORDERS_TABLE set.
The table itself is still in DynamoDB.
entries.fix: Put ORDERS_TABLE back in the Lambda environment and redeploy. There is no application patch.

entries.title: Payments URL points at staging
entries.happened: PAYMENTS_URL was set to the staging host during a production deploy. Charges hit the wrong account.
detail: The application code is the same as the last good release.
The staging host answers 200, so this does not look like a timeout.
entries.fix: Point PAYMENTS_URL back at the production host and redeploy the configuration.

entries.title: Database timeout set too low
entries.happened: DB_TIMEOUT_S was changed from 2 to 0.05. Healthy queries now raise TimeoutError.
detail: inventory-db metrics show queries finishing in under a second.
The previous environment value was 2 seconds.
entries.fix: Restore DB_TIMEOUT_S. A real inventory-db hang is a dependency, and this setting is not that.

entries.title: Checkout flag enabled without its table
entries.happened: CHECKOUT_V2 was turned on, but the v2 table name was left blank. Checkout raises KeyError on the missing setting.
detail: CHECKOUT_V2=false still uses the old path and succeeds.
No coupon code is involved in this failure.
entries.fix: Set the v2 table name, or turn CHECKOUT_V2 off, then redeploy. Do not patch the coupon lookup for this.

entries.title: Service logs shipped to the wrong group
entries.happened: LOG_GROUP was changed to a group from another stack. The alarm sees errors, and this service's log group stays empty.
detail: The other log group contains this service's request lines.
The function is still running.
entries.fix: Point LOG_GROUP back at this service and redeploy. Empty logs alone are not enough to call the incident a code defect.

entries.title: Debug logging left on after deploy
entries.happened: LOG_LEVEL was set to DEBUG in production. Each request writes the full payload and the disk fills.
detail: The error rate is still low. The disk metric is what pages.
The last deploy is the change that set DEBUG.
entries.fix: Set LOG_LEVEL back to INFO and redeploy. Then clear the debug files. This is configuration, not an application patch.

entries.title: Inventory database timeout
entries.happened: The inventory lookup waits on inventory-db and raises TimeoutError. The storefront code is waiting, not crashing on a bad line.
detail: BULK-42 is the demo sku. Other bulk skus can wait the same way.
The handler does not catch the timeout, so the request becomes a 500.
entries.fix: A person checks inventory-db. OpsPilot does not open a pull request for this.

entries.title: Legacy payment provider is slow
entries.happened: The legacy payment provider takes about 6 seconds and the latency alarm fires. The handler is waiting on the provider.
detail: provider=legacy is the slow path. The current provider returns quickly.
There is no traceback. The request eventually returns.
entries.fix: Page the payment provider owner. Do not change the order lookup because checkout latency rose.

entries.title: Inventory host does not resolve
entries.happened: DNS for inventory-db fails with Temporary failure in name resolution. The application never reaches the query.
detail: The database process is up in its own account.
Every inventory request fails together.
entries.fix: Restore the inventory-db name. There is no code change in the storefront.

entries.title: Payment provider certificate expired
entries.happened: The TLS handshake to the payment provider fails because the remote certificate expired.
detail: The error is certificate verify failed.
Calls to inventory and orders still succeed.
entries.fix: The provider rotates the certificate. The storefront trust store does not need a code patch for an expired remote cert.

entries.title: Notification queue stopped draining
entries.happened: The notify queue age climbs because the downstream mail API returns 503. The worker is retrying, not crashing.
detail: Orders and checkout still return success.
Messages become visible again after each failed send.
entries.fix: Wait for the mail API, or pause the worker. Do not patch the storefront for a downstream 503.

entries.title: Catalog throttles the storefront
entries.happened: The catalog service returns HTTP 429. Checkout fails while waiting on a price it cannot fetch.
detail: The 429 body says the catalog quota is exhausted.
A single sku in a quiet period succeeds.
entries.fix: Raise the catalog quota or slow the caller. The checkout code did not start returning 429 by itself.

entries.title: Report export runs out of memory
entries.happened: The export buffers the whole period in memory and the Lambda exits with Runtime.OutOfMemory.
detail: days=1 still fits. days=90 is the demo that crashes.
The crash is a platform out-of-memory, not an exception from a bad dict lookup.
entries.fix: Stream the export or raise the memory size. This is resource exhaustion, not a logic bug in another route.

entries.title: Database connection pool exhausted
entries.happened: Logs say the connection pool is exhausted or QueuePool limit reached. New requests time out waiting for a connection.
detail: The database is accepting connections from other services.
Restarting the process clears the page until the pool fills again.
entries.fix: Find the connection leak, or raise the pool size as a stopgap. A full disk or a pool limit is not a code defect unless a stack frame shows a leak in this repo.

entries.title: Host disk is full
entries.happened: The host disk is full. Writes fail with No space left on device, including log writes.
detail: The largest growth is the application log directory.
CPU and memory still have headroom.
entries.fix: Free disk or grow the volume, and cap the logs. Do not open a pull request unless a stack frame shows this repo writing unbounded files.

entries.title: Checkout CPU is saturated
entries.happened: CPU stays near 100 percent and checkout latency rises. The process is busy, and there is no new exception.
detail: A traffic spike started at the same minute as the alarm.
Error logs are quiet.
entries.fix: Add capacity or shed load. High CPU without an error line is not enough to propose a code change.

entries.title: Lambda concurrency quota reached
entries.happened: Invocations fail with TooManyRequestsException because the reserved concurrency quota is exhausted.
detail: The function that does run finishes normally.
The quota was lowered in the account, not in the handler.
entries.fix: Raise the concurrency quota or slow the caller. There is no handler patch.

entries.title: Orders table is throttled
entries.happened: DynamoDB returns ProvisionedThroughputExceededException on the orders table. The handler is retrying the same read.
detail: Consumed capacity is flat against the provisioned limit.
The item key in the request is valid.
entries.fix: Raise the table capacity or switch the table to on-demand. A missing item is a different incident and returns a not-found result.

entries.title: Lambda ephemeral storage is full
entries.happened: The export writes the whole file under /tmp and the Lambda ephemeral storage fills.
detail: The error text is No space left on device under /tmp.
Memory still has room, so this is not Runtime.OutOfMemory.
entries.fix: Stream the file out, or raise ephemeral storage. Do not change the order handler.

entries.title: Alarm fired with no stack
entries.happened: The error alarm fired, and the log window has no traceback and no error line from this service.
detail: The metric moved. The log filter found nothing.
A retry of the same minute also has an empty window.
entries.fix: Leave the incident for a person. Do not invent a code change or a pull request without a stack frame or an error line.

entries.title: Latency rose without an error line
entries.happened: p95 latency crossed the alarm threshold. Request logs show 200 responses and no exception text.
detail: No downstream timeout is named in the logs.
CPU and memory alarms are quiet.
entries.fix: Collect a longer window or a trace before classifying this as a code defect. A metric by itself is not grounding.

entries.title: Trace stops before the handler
entries.happened: The trace shows the load balancer and then stops. There is no application span and no log line.
detail: The target health check is failing open.
No commit in the window touches the order handler.
entries.fix: Ask for the application logs. Do not propose a patch from a trace that never entered the service.

entries.title: How OpsPilot classifies an incident
entries.happened: Every incident gets one classification: code_defect, config_regression, dependency, resource, or insufficient_evidence.
detail: code_defect is a wrong line in this repo, backed by a stack frame.
config_regression is a bad setting or a bad deploy of configuration.
dependency is a downstream system this service waits on.
resource is disk, memory, CPU, connections, or a quota.
insufficient_evidence means the logs do not support a cause yet.
entries.fix: Only a code_defect with a stack frame at a real file and line is a candidate for a pull request. The other four classifications notify a person.

entries.title: What counts as evidence
entries.happened: Evidence kinds are log_line, stack_frame, commit, and metric. A metric can color the story and cannot ground a code change by itself.
detail: A retrieved knowledge passage is background. It is not an evidence item.
A stack frame has to match a file and line that exist in the repo.
entries.fix: Cite a log line, a stack frame, or a commit when proposing a cause. Do not cite a knowledge-base passage as proof.

entries.title: When not to open a pull request
entries.happened: Disk full, connection pool exhaustion, a downstream timeout, a missing environment variable, and an alarm with no error line all look urgent and none of them is automatically a code change.
detail: config_regression is fixed by restoring the setting.
dependency and resource incidents page a person.
insufficient_evidence waits for more logs.
entries.fix: Open a pull request only for a code_defect whose suspected location is backed by a matching stack frame.

entries.title: Path from alarm to ticket
entries.happened: A CloudWatch alarm reaches EventBridge, ingest deduplicates it, CollectContext reads the log window, and the RCA step classifies the incident.
detail: Dedup holds a repeat of the same alarm for about 15 minutes.
The alarm must return to OK before it can page again.
entries.fix: After classification, a code defect can become a pull request. Every other class becomes an OpsCenter OpsItem and a notification.

entries.title: Redact secrets before saving knowledge
entries.happened: Incident notes can contain emails, tokens, and account identifiers. Those values are removed before a document is shown or stored.
detail: The preview on the incident page and the uploaded object use the same redacted text.
A merged pull request is what starts a solution ingest.
entries.fix: Keep secrets out of the knowledge base. Store the redacted markdown only.

entries.title: Log note for an unknown order
entries.happened: Log line: unhandled_exception AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'total' while reading the order map.
detail: The line also includes the route /orders/999.
No TimeoutError appears in this window.
entries.fix: The matching historical fix is to return 404 for a missing order.

entries.title: Log note for an unknown coupon
entries.happened: Log line: KeyError: 'SPRING50' in the coupon table during checkout.
detail: The sku in the same request is valid.
The payment provider was not called.
entries.fix: The matching historical fix is HTTP 400 for an unknown coupon.

entries.title: Log note for an inventory timeout
entries.happened: Log line: TimeoutError: timed out waiting for inventory-db.
detail: The line names inventory-db.
There is no AttributeError in this window.
entries.fix: The matching historical fix is to check inventory-db. Do not patch the order map.

entries.title: Log note for a report export crash
entries.happened: Platform log: Runtime.OutOfMemory during the report export. The process ends before a Python traceback is flushed.
detail: The request query includes days=90.
A shorter export in the same hour succeeded.
entries.fix: The matching historical fix is to stream the export or raise memory.

entries.title: Log note for a full connection pool
entries.happened: Log line: sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out.
detail: The phrase connection pool appears in the same line.
The database error is a wait, not a syntax error.
entries.fix: The matching historical fix is to find the leak or raise the pool size.

entries.title: Log note for a full disk
entries.happened: Log line: OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device.
detail: The path is the application log file.
df reports the volume at 100 percent.
entries.fix: The matching historical fix is to free disk. This log line is not a stack frame in application logic.

entries.title: Log note for a missing table setting
entries.happened: Log line: KeyError: 'ORDERS_TABLE' while reading the environment at startup.
detail: The line is emitted before the first request handler runs.
The orders table still exists.
entries.fix: The matching historical fix is to restore the ORDERS_TABLE environment variable.
